pr_title: Fix `Cache::NullStore` with local caching for repeated reads
pr_body:
Fixes #45690, check it for the details.

It is reproducible by configuring null cache store and calling the same read operation (like `Rails.cache.read_multi("foo", "bar")`) multiple times. After the first call, the local cache will include all the keys with nils. In the second, we retrieve this nils and trying to call `.value` on it.

So I think, in the original issue one thread called read once, and another thread - again, so hence the error.

cc @CodingAnarchy @byroot

issue_context.title: NullStore cache randomly blows up in asynchronous cases
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

This appears to be an esoteric bug that I found in an edge case while running asynchronous code that all queried the `NullStore` cache (which was empty).

I couldn't come up with a way to replicate without loading the entire application, nor by loading the application on another machine, but I did manage to fix it locally by adding a safe navigation operator on: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/752b566152ca3e8daf4804c90777cc1a01d003f6/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb#L135

What I'm wondering is if this is a sensible thing to adjust to avoid this weird case.

### Expected behavior

Cache value should return `nil` and fall through to continuing code.

### Actual behavior

```ruby
undefined method `value' for nil:NilClass
   
                   deserialize_entry(payload).value
                                              ^^^^^
 /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:127:in `block in read_multi_entries'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:126:in `transform_values!'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb:126:in `read_multi_entries'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache.rb:425:in `block in read_multi'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache.rb:778:in `block in instrument'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/notifications.rb:208:in `instrument'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache.rb:778:in `instrument'
    /Users/mtanous/.gem/ruby/3.1.2/gems/activesupport-7.0.3.1/lib/active_support/cache.rb:424:in `read_multi'
16156 /Users/mtanous/src/github.com/Shopify/grid-next/app/lib/cache.rb:35:in `read_multi'
```

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.0.3.1

**Ruby version**: 3.1.2
comments:
> while running asynchronous code that all queried the `NullStore` cache

Can you share more details about that asynchronous code, maybe with some code snippets?

The error is occurring in this bit of code (note that I have removed some proprietary identifiers and renamed some methods):

```ruby
      def cache
        @_cache ||= begin
          cache_keys = @fields.map do |field|
            cache_key(field)
          end
          # Marked as unsafe because of Sorbet's poor support for splats of unknown length
          T.unsafe(Rails.cache).read_multi(*cache_keys) # <== This line is what breaks
        end
      end

      def date_params(field, with_previous_week: false)
        raise ArgumentError, "Dates not set" unless @end_date.present? && @start_date.present?

        cache_key = cache_key(field)
        # .default_date causes a db query but should only happen in the rare case
        # when the cache has been wiped manually and before the job has been run again.
        date =
          cache[cache_key] || default_date(field)
        time_span = @end_date - @start_date
        end_date = [@end_date, date].min
        start_date = end_date - time_span

        dates = {
          start_date: start_date,
          end_date: end_date,
        }

        return dates unless with_previous_week

        dates.merge({ start_date_week_before: start_date - 1.week })
      end
```

The `date_params` method is being called to obtain the two date values for other code. The call to `cache[cache_key]` that initially fetches the cache via `read_multi` throws the error above.

Am I missing something, or can you share some details about the asynchronous usage of this code you mentioned?

The problem you described may be somehow related to the thread unsafety of the local cache, used in the `NullStore`: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b623494a29d620f67f4093f60aba93705db02464/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb#L29-L31

It is wrapped in a block with a semaphore from the `async` gem:

``` ruby
semaphore = Async::Semaphore.new(concurrent_executions, parent: barrier)
semaphore.async do |task|
   // code that executes these calls
end
```

The goal here is to generate some SQL and then execute it asynchronously against a database. What is fetched from the cache is a date (or `nil`, in which case we fall back to a default). In the development environment (where this was failing for me), the cache is (generally) empty and we expect the fall back.

I understand the `LocalStore` cache is not thread-safe (in production, this connects to a Memcached instance instead). I would expect, however, that the lack of thread-safety entails that race conditions may give me the wrong results, not break the application unexpectedly. In this case, there _are no writes to the cache_. It is completely empty, but it is breaking the application. (It is also a `NullStore`, which on its face seems like it should just return `nil` for anything that isn't cached for that single thread.)

Putting the safe navigation operator in that line resolves the issue entirely, at least for this case.

review_comments:
```suggestion
              deserialize_entry(payload).value unless payload.nil?
```

if I'm not mistaken, `payload` is `nil` here, so might as well skip `deserialize_entry`
Actually nevermind, design wise it's best not to assume anything about how a nil payload may be deserialized.
